question: Which of the following dances was traditionally performed by male monks in monasteries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form of India that originated in the state of Assam.
 
• This dance was traditionally performed by **male monks** in the **Vaishnavite monasteries** called **Sattras**.
 
• **Sattriya** dance was introduced in the 15th century by the saint-scholar **Sankardev** as a medium for **religious expression and devotion**.
 
• The dance is characterized by its **spiritual themes**, including tales from the life of Lord Krishna and other religious stories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sankardev**:

 
 
• He was a 15th-16th century saint-scholar, poet, playwright, and social-religious reformer in Assam.
 
• Sankardev is credited with the creation and propagation of the **Neo-Vaishnavite movement** in Assam.
 
 
 
• **Sattras**:
 
 
• Sattras are **Vaishnavite monasteries** that were established by Sankardev and his followers to promote the Neo-Vaishnavite culture and religion.
 
• These institutions are centers of religious, cultural, and educational activities in Assam.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dances of India**:
 
 
• **Kathakali**: A classical dance form from Kerala known for its elaborate costumes and dramatic performances.
 
• **Kuchipudi**: A classical dance from Andhra Pradesh, known for its graceful movements and strong narrative character.
 
• **Odissi**: A classical dance form from Odisha, characterized by its sculpturesque poses and fluid movements.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism**:
 
 
• It is one of the major traditions within Hinduism that worships Vishnu and his avatars, primarily Rama and Krishna.
 
• Vaishnavism emphasizes the devotion (bhakti) towards Vishnu as the Supreme God.
